            title: 'SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
              Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability'
            why_it_matters: ''
            parent_issue_id: null
            fact_ids: []
            disposition: null
          questions:
          - question_id: Q-SAR
            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
              been reviewed, and what did they reveal?
            consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they
              can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and
              could affect the deal itself.
            state: answered
            answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
              in diligence.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-070aec
          - question_id: Q-KYC
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
              what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay's own BSA/AML customer identification
              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance
              gap depends on how Mosaic plans to satisfy its own CIP/recordkeeping
              obligations for these users.
            state: answered
            answer: It is not yet known whether Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program permits
              reliance on Harbor's prior KYC; compliance must confirm.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-620c62
          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
              what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
              before onboarding those customers?
            consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.
            state: answered
            answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses
              for the four new markets.
            answer_kind: reported_fact
            linked_fact_ids:
            - FACT-20260909-771ee1
          - question_id: Q-BONUS
            text: How is the $50 welcome bonus structured?
            consequence: The structure determines whether the bonus triggers consumer
              disclosure, funds-flow, or state promotional requirements.
            state: left_open
            answer: null
            answer_kind: null

            passages: &id032
            - start: 0
              end: 817
              text: '# Issues and workstreams


                - Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
                the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
                the acquisition

                - BSA/AML and KYC: whether relying on Harbor''s prior KYC (with missing
                underlying documents for pre-2023 users) satisfies Mosaic Relay''s
                independent CIP/AML obligations

                - SAR and alert handling: obligations to review, file, and manage
                Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and SARs, and successor liability

                - Monitoring vendor transition: continuity of transaction monitoring
                when the SaaS contract terminates at close

                - Marketing compliance: the $50 welcome bonus offer and any state
                money transmission or consumer protection implications

                - Customer account, contract, and data-transfer rights <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-af341445a7af4c06
                -->

                '

            - start: 0
              end: 3962
              text: '# Known Facts


                - Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
                weeks out).

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance and full access to Mosaic''s product set.

                - Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC''d by
                Harbor.

                - Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
                Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new
                markets.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
                has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
                for users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor''s transaction feed
                at Mosaic''s engine on day 1.

                - Marketing wants a ''Welcome'' campaign with a $50 bonus on first
                transfer, launching close+1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.

                - Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
                Mosaic Relay''s app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account
                and balance.

                - Plan is no re-verification of Harbor''s existing KYC; Harbor users
                were already KYC''d.

                - Harbor''s KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail
                results exist for everyone but underlying documents are missing for
                users onboarded before 2023.

                - Harbor''s transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
                terminates at close; plan is to repoint the transaction feed to Mosaic
                Relay''s engine on day 1.

                - Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and ''a handful'' of SARs from
                the last year at Harbor; none have been read yet.

                - How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
                buys Harbor''s assets)

                - Does Mosaic Relay''s AML/CIP program currently permit relying on
                another institution''s prior KYC without re-verification, or is re-verification
                required? — Not sure / need to check with compliance

                - What is known about Harbor''s ~40 open alerts and the SARs from
                the last year? — Nothing reviewed yet — still in diligence

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does
                Mosaic Relay plan to operate under Harbor''s existing licenses or
                apply for its own? — Use/assume Harbor''s licenses

                - For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,
                what is the plan to satisfy Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML customer identification
                and recordkeeping obligations? — It is not yet known whether Mosaic
                Relay''s AML/CIP program permits reliance on Harbor''s prior KYC;
                compliance must confirm.

                - Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year
                been reviewed, and what did they reveal? — The open alerts and SAR
                history have not been reviewed and remain in diligence.

                - For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,
                what is the plan for state money transmission licensing or approval
                before onboarding those customers? — Mosaic Relay currently plans
                to use or assume Harbor''s licenses for the four new markets.


                ## Assumptions


                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay''s existing money transmission licenses
                and Harbor''s MTLs are transferable or can be maintained through the
                acquisition without new state approval

                - [Assumption] The KYC pass/fail results are sufficient to satisfy
                Mosaic Relay''s own BSA/AML program obligations without the underlying
                documents

                - [Assumption] The transaction monitoring repoint can be completed
                and validated before close without a monitoring gap

                - [Assumption] Harbor Pay is a licensed money transmitter subject
                to state MTL regimes and federal BSA/AML obligations (not yet confirmed).

                - [Assumption] Mosaic Relay is itself a licensed money transmitter
                in 41 states (per the request).

                - [Assumption] The acquisition is structured as an asset or stock
                purchase, which affects whether Harbor''s licenses and SAR/alert obligations
                transfer (structure not yet confirmed).

                '

            passages: &id034
            - start: 0
              end: 6000
              text: '# Harbor 2 matter dossier


                ## Current position


                The Harbor Pay migration needs legal and compliance review before
                the planned Nov 15 close. This is the accepted working view. No decision
                has been recorded.


                This draft recommends continuing close preparation but making the
                day-one service migration conditional. Mosaic should not give all
                Harbor users full access until:


                1. Mosaic has documented authority for each post-close service in
                each affected state.

                2. Compliance confirms that Mosaic may rely on Harbor’s know-your-customer
                (KYC) results, or defines and completes remediation.

                3. Authorized reviewers assess Harbor’s open alerts and suspicious
                activity report (SAR) history.

                4. Mosaic tests the replacement transaction-monitoring feed and finds
                no material coverage gap.


                If a condition is not met, Mosaic should hold the affected state launch,
                restrict affected accounts, or delay full product access. The $50
                welcome bonus should also wait for review of its structure, terms,
                funding, and disclosures.


                The saved material does not establish that the acquisition close itself
                must wait. However, the unread alerts and SAR history could affect
                deal terms, risk allocation, or the decision to close.


                ### Assumptions used


                - Harbor is subject to the state money-transmission and federal anti-money-laundering
                requirements discussed below. The licensing, KYC, alert, and monitoring
                conclusions depend on this unverified legal premise.

                - Mosaic will become the operating provider when Harbor users receive
                a unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products.
                The licensing analysis depends on this inference.

                - The analysis does not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that
                Harbor’s KYC results satisfy Mosaic’s program, or that the monitoring
                transition will work without a gap.


                ### Record conflicts


                - Harbor reportedly has licenses in 38 states, Mosaic has licenses
                in 41 states, and the combined footprint is 44 states. A 44-state
                footprint is three states larger than Mosaic’s 41-state footprint,
                but the record says the acquisition opens four new markets. The license
                lists and the intended meaning of “market” are needed. Until then,
                the states requiring separate authority cannot be identified reliably.

                - Matter metadata gives a target date of `2026-09-11`. The reported
                close is “Nov 15,” approximately ten weeks after the Sept. 9 intake.
                A saved hypothetical uses November 15, 2026, but that does not establish
                the actual closing year. The operative close date and year remain
                unresolved.


                ## Decision question


                Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
                before the Nov 15 close?


                ## Issues


                <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045 -->

                ### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate
                under the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
                the acquisition


                **Current answer**


                Mosaic should not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets
                that automatically move to Mosaic through the reported asset purchase.
                Mosaic should not start regulated services in a state unless it has
                documented authority for its complete post-close activity.


                The acquisition close and the service launch can be managed as separate
                milestones. If authority is not established, the present fallback
                is to hold the affected state launch or restrict regulated functions.


                **Rule and support**


                Saved research concludes that the answer must be determined state
                by state. The review must cover Mosaic’s authority, transaction notices
                or approvals, interim operations, outstanding customer obligations,
                and Harbor’s license surrender.


                Four sources were retrieved, but no operative passage was selected,
                read, or verified. They do not establish the rule in any affected
                state:


                - [Money transmission research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)

                - [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538]

                - [source:SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4]

                - [source:SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413]

                - [source:SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200]


                The model act is not proof of any state’s adopted law. The premise
                that an asset purchase does not automatically give Mosaic Harbor’s
                operating authority remains an unverified state-law conclusion.


                **Application**


                Mosaic plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in the new markets.
                The planned unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to
                Mosaic products indicate that Mosaic may become the actual provider.
                If so, keeping Harbor’s entity or licenses active might not authorize
                Mosaic’s conduct.


                Harbor could remain the licensed provider during a transition only
                if customer contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses, bonds,
                records, and applicable state rules support that result. The documents
                and actual operations must match.


                A partner bank holding funds would not alone resolve the issue. The
                analysis still depends on who contracts with users, controls transfers,
                owes repayment, records balances, resolves errors, and performs regulated
                duties.


                **Next step**


                Identify the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare a state matrix.
                For each state, determine Mosaic’s authority, required filings or
                approvals, operation while an application is pending, treatment of
                customer obligations, Harbor’s run-off duties, and the launch restriction
                needed if authority is not established.


                <!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start -->

                <details>

                <summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>


                Preserved research snapshot. Its facts and assumptions may predate
                later records. Use the current answer above for application to the
                current matter.


                Do not rely on transferability without an applicable state rule, approval,
                or written regulator position.


                The answer must be determined state by state and must cover more than
                technical change-of-control rules.


                This path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider and
                the relevant states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account
                design may conflict with that position.


                T'

          4. Mosaic tests the replacement transaction-monitoring feed and finds no
          material coverage gap.


          If a condition is not met, Mosaic should hold the affected state launch,
          restrict affected accounts, or delay full product access. The $50 welcome
          bonus should also wait for review of its structure, terms, funding, and
          disclosures.


          The saved material does not establish that the acquisition close itself
          must wait. However, the unread alerts and SAR history could affect deal
          terms, risk allocation, or the decision to close.


          ### Assumptions used


          - Harbor is subject to the state money-transmission and federal anti-money-laundering
          requirements discussed below. The licensing, KYC, alert, and monitoring
          conclusions depend on this unverified legal premise.

          - Mosaic will become the operating provider when Harbor users receive a
          unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products.
          The licensing analysis depends on this inference.

          - The analysis does not assume that Harbor’s licenses transfer, that Harbor’s
          KYC results satisfy Mosaic’s program, or that the monitoring transition
          will work without a gap.


          ### Record conflicts


          - Harbor reportedly has licenses in 38 states, Mosaic has licenses in 41
          states, and the combined footprint is 44 states. A 44-state footprint is
          three states larger than Mosaic’s 41-state footprint, but the record says
          the acquisition opens four new markets. The license lists and the intended
          meaning of “market” are needed. Until then, the states requiring separate
          authority cannot be identified reliably.

          - Matter metadata gives a target date of `2026-09-11`. The reported close
          is “Nov 15,” approximately ten weeks after the Sept. 9 intake. A saved hypothetical
          uses November 15, 2026, but that does not establish the actual closing year.
          The operative close date and year remain unresolved.


          ## Decision question


          Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal review
          before the Nov 15 close?


          ## Issues


          <!-- issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045 -->

          ### Money transmission licensing: whether Mosaic Relay can operate under
          the combined 44-state footprint and whether Harbor''s MTLs transfer/survive
          the acquisition


          **Current answer**


          Mosaic should not treat Harbor’s money transmitter licenses as assets that
          automatically move to Mosaic through the reported asset purchase. Mosaic
          should not start regulated services in a state unless it has documented
          authority for its complete post-close activity.


          The acquisition close and the service launch can be managed as separate
          milestones. If authority is not established, the present fallback is to
          hold the affected state launch or restrict regulated functions.


          **Rule and support**


          Saved research concludes that the answer must be determined state by state.
          The review must cover Mosaic’s authority, transaction notices or approvals,
          interim operations, outstanding customer obligations, and Harbor’s license
          surrender.


          Four sources were retrieved, but no operative passage was selected, read,
          or verified. They do not establish the rule in any affected state:


          - [Money transmission research packet](03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/RES-20260911-0a5f07.md)

          - [source:SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538]

          - [source:SRC-71b20ecf65825d6522c4]

          - [source:SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413]

          - [source:SRC-b48d8d40f5a0cfe9a200]


          The model act is not proof of any state’s adopted law. The premise that
          an asset purchase does not automatically give Mosaic Harbor’s operating
          authority remains an unverified state-law conclusion.


          **Application**


          Mosaic plans to use or assume Harbor’s licenses in the new markets. The
          planned unified Mosaic account, combined balance, and access to Mosaic products
          indicate that Mosaic may become the actual provider. If so, keeping Harbor’s
          entity or licenses active might not authorize Mosaic’s conduct.


          Harbor could remain the licensed provider during a transition only if customer
          contracts, funds flow, operating control, licenses, bonds, records, and
          applicable state rules support that result. The documents and actual operations
          must match.


          A partner bank holding funds would not alone resolve the issue. The analysis
          still depends on who contracts with users, controls transfers, owes repayment,
          records balances, resolves errors, and performs regulated duties.


          **Next step**


          Identify the Harbor-only jurisdictions and prepare a state matrix. For each
          state, determine Mosaic’s authority, required filings or approvals, operation
          while an application is pending, treatment of customer obligations, Harbor’s
          run-off duties, and the launch restriction needed if authority is not established.


          <!-- retained-issue:ISS-c9d7c39f63-94e42e2b38090045:start -->

          <details>

          <summary>Saved research and prior analysis</summary>


          Preserved research snapshot. Its facts and assumptions may predate later
          records. Use the current answer above for application to the current matter.


          Do not rely on transferability without an applicable state rule, approval,
          or written regulator position.


          The answer must be determined state by state and must cover more than technical
          change-of-control rules.


          This path is possible only if Harbor remains the real provider and the relevant
          states permit the arrangement. The unified Mosaic account design may conflict
          with that position.


          T'

          business_question:
            question_id: BQ-c9d7c39f6380eb60
            text: Does any part of the Harbor Pay acquisition migration need legal
              review before the Nov 15 close?
            revision: legacy:6abf4a45ae87313af8db04b89d546e0e1a1c6137341b3d3c0d159c66cf64d54c
          facts:
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-182bcc
            text: Mosaic Relay is acquiring Harbor Pay; close targeted Nov 15 (~10
              weeks out).
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-551367
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into
              Mosaic Relay's app on day 1 post-close, with one unified account and
              balance and full access to Mosaic's product set.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9a0c61
            text: Plan is no re-verification; Harbor users were already KYC'd by Harbor.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-33293c
            text: Harbor holds money transmitter licenses (MTLs) in 38 states; Mosaic
              Relay holds 41; combined footprint is 44 states, opening four new markets.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-aea8ec
            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; Mosaic
              has pass/fail results for everyone but not the underlying documents
              for users onboarded before 2023.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-073838
            text: Harbor's transaction monitoring is a third-party SaaS whose contract
              terminates at close; plan is to repoint Harbor's transaction feed at
              Mosaic's engine on day 1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-19aebc
            text: Marketing wants a 'Welcome' campaign with a $50 bonus on first transfer,
              launching close+1.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-adf2cb
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the
              last year at Harbor; nobody has read them yet.
            source_ids:
            - REQ-20260909-283892
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-4c1fd8
            text: Migration moves 240k consumer users and 12k business accounts into

            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f2c49f
            text: Plan is no re-verification of Harbor's existing KYC; Harbor users

            origin: null

            text: Harbor's KYC ran through a vendor that shut down in 2024; pass/fail

          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-9f7bde
            text: Diligence flagged ~40 open alerts and 'a handful' of SARs from the

            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-9835ba
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-ed9f06
            text: How is the Harbor Pay acquisition structured? — Asset purchase (Mosaic
              buys Harbor's assets)
            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-b5e71e
            text: Does Mosaic Relay's AML/CIP program currently permit relying on

            source_ids:
            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-849b00
            text: What is known about Harbor's ~40 open alerts and the SARs from the

            - MSG-20260909-2e549e
            origin: null
            verification_status: null
          - fact_id: FACT-20260909-f0fb01
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined footprint, does

            origin: null
            verification_status: null

            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,

            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year

            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,

            source_ids:

            origin: null
            verification_status: null

          questions:

            text: Have the ~40 open alerts and the handful of SARs from the last year

            consequence: Unread open alerts and SARs are the highest-risk item; they
              can create BSA/AML exposure that must be addressed before close and

            state: answered
            answer: The open alerts and SAR history have not been reviewed and remain
              in diligence.

            linked_fact_ids:

          - question_id: Q-KYC
            text: For the pre-2023 Harbor users with no underlying KYC documents,

              and recordkeeping obligations?
            consequence: Whether the missing underlying documents create a compliance

            state: answered

          - question_id: Q-MTL
            text: For the four new markets opened by the combined license footprint,

              before onboarding those customers?
            consequence: Whether the four new markets can be served at close depends
              on license transferability and state approval, which is a gating regulatory
              question.
            state: answered
            answer: Mosaic Relay currently plans to use or assume Harbor's licenses

            - &id038

              section_label: null
              body_hash: 5b5d2f6c388b9bcf98252d205bb001dbdce26951229e0e6896dfecf0358be545
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000014.md
              text: "14 \n \nARTICLE V \nMoney Transmission Licenses \nSection 5.01
                License Required. \n(a) \nA person may not engage in the business
                of money transmission or \nadvertise, solicit, or hold itself out
                as providing money transmission unless the person is licensed \nunder
                this [Act]; \n(b) \n[Section 5.01(a)] does not apply to: \n(1) \nA
                person that is an authorized delegate of a person licensed under \nthis
                [Act] acting within the scope of authority conferred by a written
                contract with the \nlicensee; or \n(2) \nA person that is exempt pursuant
                to [Section 3.01] and does not \nengage in money transmission outside
                the scope of such exemption. \n(c) \nA license issued under [Section
                5.05] is not transferable or assignable. \nSection 5.02 Consistent
                State Licensing. \n(a) \nTo establish consistent licensing between
                [this state] and other states, the \n[Commissioner] is authorized
                and encouraged to: \n(1) \nimplement all licensing provisions of this
                [Act] in a manner that is \nconsistent with other states that have
                adopted this [Act]or multistate licensing processes; \nand \n(2) \nparticipate
                in nationwide protocols for licensing cooperation and \ncoordination
                among state regulators provided that such protocols are consistent
                with this \n[Act]. \n(b) \nIn order to fulfill the purposes of this
                [Act], the [Commissioner] is \nauthorized and encouraged to establish
                relationships or contracts with NMLS or other entities \ndesignated
                by NMLS to enable the [Commissioner] to: \n(1) \ncollect and maintain
                records; \n(2) \ncoordinate multistate licensing processes and supervision
                processes; \n(3) \nprocess fees; and \n(4) \nfacilitate communication
                between [state] and licensees or other \npersons subject to this [Act].
                \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize
                NMLS for all \naspects of licensing in accordance with this [Act],
                including but not limited to, license applications, \napplications
                for acquisitions of control, surety bonds, reporting, criminal history
                background\n"
            - &id039
              unit_id: p000021
              start: 0
              end: 2389
              page_number: 21
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 5638ae03ab2c6c110a80e30639b8ccd42a1c585fdc2818a38e4f2f0fc69a5e06
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000021.md
              text: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. The renewal
                report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material change
                in information submitted by the licensee in its original license \napplication
                which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe [Commissioner]
                for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate. \n(d)
                \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
                to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality is
                consistent with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of
                License. \n(a) \nIf a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications
                or satisfy the \nrequirements that apply to an applicant for a new
                money transmission license, the [Commissioner] \nmay suspend or revoke
                the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures established
                by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension
                or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license
                must demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission
                licensee must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01,
                10.02, and 10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control
                and Change of Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control.
                \n(a) \nAny person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
                to acquire control \nof a licensee shall obtain the written approval
                of the [Commissioner] prior to acquiring control. \nAn individual
                is not deemed to acquire control of a licensee and is not subject
                to these acquisition \nof control provisions when that individual
                becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of \nbusiness. \n(b)
                \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire
                control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee: \n(1)
                \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the
                \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with
                the request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner]
                may permit a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting
                in concert, to submit some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner]
                pursuant to [Section 6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application
                required by [Section 6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired
                by [Section 5.04] for any new key individuals that have not previously
                completed the \nrequirements of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"
            - &id040
              unit_id: p000022
              start: 0
              end: 2612
              page_number: 22
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
              text: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
                under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address
                all of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered
                complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant
                in a record of \nthe date on which the application was determined
                to be complete and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve
                or deny the application within 60 \ndays after the completion date;
                or \n(2) \nif the application is not approved or denied within 60
                days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A) \nthe application is approved;
                and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons acting in concert, are
                not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe [Commissioner]
                may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f) \nA determination
                by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete and \nis accepted
                for processing means only that the application, on its face, appears
                to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters that
                are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application
                or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an
                application is filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)],
                the [Commissioner] shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility,
                financial \nand business experience, character, and general fitness
                of the person, or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to
                acquire control. The [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of
                control \npursuant to this [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds
                that all of the following conditions have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1)
                \nThe requirements of subsections (b) and (d) have been met, as \napplicable;
                and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and responsibility, financial
                and business \nexperience, competence, character, and general fitness
                of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert, seeking to
                acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand
                general fitness of the key individuals and persons that would be in
                control of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate
                that it is in the interest of the public to \npermit the person, or
                group of persons acting in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h)
                \nIf an applicant avails itself or is otherwise subject to a multistate
                licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS will accommodate and streamline
                the process of communicating when applications are \nreceived and
                when states consider them to have been complete. The intent of this
                Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an application
                is determined to be complete.\n"
            - &id041
              unit_id: p000023
              start: 0
              end: 2523
              page_number: 23
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 83a664c778fbc9de0b4d13270e2a918f6488b461db1a6617e3d36032163068ca
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000023.md
              text: "23 \n \nprocess: \n(1) \nthe [Commissioner] is authorized and
                encouraged to accept the \ninvestigation results of a lead investigative
                state for the purpose of [Section 6.01(g)] if the \nlead investigative
                state has sufficient staffing, expertise, and minimum standards; or
                \n(2) \nif [state] is a lead investigative state, the [Commissioner]
                is \nauthorized and encouraged to investigate the applicant pursuant
                to [Section 6.01(g)] and \nthe timeframes established by agreement
                through the multistate licensing process. \n(i) \nThe [Commissioner]
                shall issue a formal written notice of the denial of an \napplication
                to acquire control within thirty (30) days of the decision to deny
                the application. The \n[Commissioner] shall set forth in the notice
                of denial the specific reasons for the denial of the \napplication.
                An applicant whose application is denied by the [Commissioner] under
                this [Section \n6.01(i)] may appeal within thirty (30) days16 after
                receipt of the written notice of the denial \n[pursuant to state administrative
                law procedures]. \n(j) \nThe requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and
                (b)] do not apply to any of the \nfollowing: \n(1) \nA person that
                acts as a proxy for the sole purpose of voting at a \ndesignated meeting
                of the shareholders or holders of voting shares or voting interests
                of a \nlicensee or a person in control of a licensee; \n(2) \nA person
                that acquires control of a licensee by devise or descent; \n(3) \nA
                person that acquires control of a licensee as a personal \nrepresentative,
                custodian, guardian, conservator, or trustee, or as an officer appointed
                by a \ncourt of competent jurisdiction or by operation of law; \n(4)
                \nA person that is exempt under [Section 3.01(g)]; \n(5) \nA person
                that the [Commissioner] determines is not subject to \n[Section 6.01(a)]
                based on the public interest; \n(6) \nA public offering of securities
                of a licensee or a person in control of \na licensee; or \n(7) \nAn
                internal reorganization of a person in control of the licensee \nwhere
                the ultimate person in control of the licensee remains the same. \n(k)
                \nPersons in [Sections 6.01(j)(2), (3), (4), (6), (7)] in cooperation
                with the \nlicensee shall notify the [Commissioner] within [15] days
                after the acquisition of control.17 \n \n16 Commentary: Administrative
                procedures for challenging a departmental decision may be derived
                from other \naspects of state law. In such a case, this Act should
                be adjusted to reflect the relevant administrative process. \n17 Commentary:
                Notice is satisfied upon updating the licensee’s NMLS record.\n"
            - &id042
              unit_id: p000024
              start: 0
              end: 2799
              page_number: 24
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 4732d9c2b053975a4d3cb27db8e99faa4baf45f71eb350fa519e31b5890ac680
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000024.md
              text: "24 \n \n(l) \nStreamlined Acquisition of Control \n(1) \nThe
                requirements of [Section 6.01(a) and (b)] do not apply to a \nperson
                that has complied with and received approval to engage in money transmission
                \nunder this [Act] or was identified as a person in control in a prior
                application filed with and \napproved by the [Commissioner] or by
                an MSB accredited state pursuant to a multistate \nlicensing process,
                provided that: \n(A) \nthe person has not had a license revoked or
                suspended or \ncontrolled a licensee that has had a license revoked
                or suspended while the person \nwas in control of the licensee in
                the previous 5-years; \n(B) \nif the person is a licensee, the person
                is well managed and \nhas received at least a satisfactory rating
                for compliance at its most recent \nexamination by an MSB accredited
                state if such rating was given; \n(C) \nthe licensee to be acquired
                is projected to meet the \nrequirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
                and 10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition \nof control is completed,
                and if the person acquiring control is a licensee, that \nlicensee
                is also projected to meet the requirements of [Sections 10.01, 10.02,
                and \n10.03] of this [Act] after the acquisition of control is completed;
                \n(D) \nthe licensee to be acquired will not implement any material
                \nchanges to its business plan as a result of the acquisition of control,
                and if the person \nacquiring control is a licensee, that licensee
                also will not implement any material \nchanges to its business plan
                as a result of the acquisition of control;  and \n(E) \nthe person
                provides notice of the acquisition in cooperation \nwith the licensee
                and attests to [Section 6.01(l)(1)(A), (B), (C), and (D)] in a form
                \nand in a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner]. \n(2) \nIf the
                notice is not disapproved within 30 days after the date on \nwhich
                the notice was determined to be complete, the notice is deemed approved.
                \n(m) \nBefore filing an application for approval to acquire control
                of a licensee a \nperson may request in writing a determination from
                the [Commissioner] as to whether the person \nwould be considered
                a person in control of a licensee upon consummation of a proposed
                \ntransaction. If the [Commissioner] determines that the person would
                not be a person in control of \na licensee, the proposed Person and
                transaction is not subject to the requirements of [Section \n6.01(a)
                and (b)] of this [Act]. \n(n) \nIf a multistate licensing process
                includes a determination pursuant to \n[Section 6.01(m)] and an applicant
                avails itself or is otherwise subject to the multistate licensing
                \nprocess: \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged
                to accept the \ncontrol determination of a lead investigative state
                with sufficient staffing, expertise, and \nminimum standards for the
                purpose of [Section 6.01(m)]; or\n"
            - &id043
              unit_id: p000004
              start: 298
              end: 2509
              page_number: 4
              section_label: null
              body_hash: 2245b178c49fc1f157bf15c133c59f8fcfe9abdf43f0bf94df397229a7889584
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000004.md
              text: "ly for goods or services provided by the issuer or its affiliate
                or franchisees of the issuer \nor its affiliate, except to the extent
                required by applicable law to be redeemable in cash for its cash \nvalue;
                \n(f) \n\"Control\" means \n(1) \n(A) the power to vote, directly
                or indirectly, at least 25 percent of \nthe outstanding voting shares
                or voting interests of a licensee or person in control of a \nlicensee;
                \n(B) \nthe power to elect or appoint a majority of key individuals
                or \nexecutive officers, managers, directors, trustees, or other persons
                exercising \nmanagerial authority of a person in control of a licensee;
                or \n(C) \nthe power to exercise, directly or indirectly, a controlling
                \ninfluence over the management or policies of a licensee or person
                in control of a \nlicensee. \n(2) \nRebuttable Presumption of Control.
                \n(A) \nA person is presumed to exercise a controlling influence \nwhen
                the person holds the power to vote, directly or indirectly, at least
                10 percent \nof the outstanding voting shares or voting interests
                of a licensee or person in control \nof a licensee.2 \n(B) \nA person
                presumed to exercise a controlling influence as \ndefined by this
                [Section 2.01(f)] can rebut the presumption of control if the person
                \nis a passive investor. \n(3) \nFor purposes of determining the percentage
                of a person controlled \nby any other person, the person's interest
                shall be aggregated with the interest of any other \nimmediate family
                member, including the person's spouse, parents, children, siblings,
                \nmothers- and fathers-in law, sons- and daughters-in-law, brothers-
                and sisters-in-law, and \nany other person who shares such person's
                home. \n(g) \n\"Eligible rating\" shall mean a credit rating of any
                of the three highest rating \ncategories provided by an eligible rating
                service, whereby each category may include rating \n \n2 Commentary:
                The obligation to rebut control rests exclusively with the person
                acquiring ≥10% of the outstanding \nvoting shares or voting interests
                of a licensee or person in control of a licensee.  It is not the responsibility
                of the \nlicensee to rebut control.  This is consistent with Section
                601(a) of the Act which requires the person acquiring control \nto
                obtain prior approval.\n"
            - &id044
              unit_id: p000030
              start: 0
              end: 2670
              page_number: 30

              body_hash: 0d032292dd6b007bb0772b41f7c3f21512a56d4557c8c7b69696774b6248c842
              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000030.md
              text: "30 \n \n(1) \nappoint the person signing the contract as the
                licensee's authorized \ndelegate with the authority to conduct money
                transmission on behalf of the licensee; \n(2) \nset forth the nature
                and scope of the relationship between the \nlicensee and the authorized
                delegate and the respective rights and responsibilities of the \nparties;
                \n(3) \nrequire the authorized delegate to agree to fully comply with
                all \napplicable state and federal laws, rules, and regulations pertaining
                to money transmission, \nincluding this [Act] and regulations implementing
                this [Act], relevant provisions of the \nBank Secrecy Act and the
                USA PATRIOT ACT; \n(4) \nrequire the authorized delegate to remit
                and handle money and \nmonetary value in accordance with the terms
                of the contract between the licensee and the \nauthorized delegate;
                \n(5) \nimpose a trust on money and monetary value net of fees received
                for \nmoney transmission for the benefit of the licensee; \n(6) \nrequire
                the authorized delegate to prepare and maintain records as \nrequired
                by this [Act] or regulations implementing this [Act], or as reasonably
                requested \nby the [Commissioner]; \n(7) \nacknowledge that the authorized
                delegate consents to examination \nor investigation by the [Commissioner];
                \n(8) \nstate that the licensee is subject to regulation by the [Commissioner]
                \nand that, as part of that regulation, the [Commissioner] may suspend
                or revoke an \nauthorized delegate designation or require the licensee
                to terminate an authorized delegate \ndesignation; and \n(9) \n(9)
                \ acknowledge receipt of the written policies and procedures \nrequired
                under [Section 8.01(b)(1)]. \n(e) \nIf the licensee's license is suspended,
                revoked, surrendered, or expired, the \nlicensee must, within five
                (5) business days, provide documentation to the [Commissioner] that
                \nthe licensee has notified all applicable authorized delegates of
                the licensee whose names are in a \nrecord filed with the [Commissioner]
                of the suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a \nlicense.
                Upon suspension, revocation, surrender, or expiration of a license,
                applicable authorized \ndelegates shall immediately cease to provide
                money transmission as an authorized delegate of the \nlicensee. \n(f)
                \nAn authorized delegate of a licensee holds in trust for the benefit
                of the \nlicensee all money net of fees received from money transmission.
                \ If any authorized delegate \ncommingles any funds received from
                money transmission with any other funds or property owned \nor controlled
                by the authorized delegate, all commingled funds and other property
                shall be \nconsidered held in trust in favor of the licensee in an
                amount equal to the amount of money net of\n"

              text: "31 \n \nfees received from money transmission.22 \n(g) \nAn authorized
                delegate may not use a subdelegate to conduct money \ntransmission
                on behalf of a licensee. \nSection 8.02 Unauthorized Activities \nA
                person shall not engage in the business of money transmission on behalf
                of a person \nnot licensed under this [Act]  or not exempt pursuant
                to [Article III] of this [Act]. A person that \nengages in such activity
                provides money transmission to the same extent as if the person were
                a \nlicensee, and shall be jointly and severally liable with the unlicensed
                or nonexempt person. \nSection 8.03 [Optional]: Prohibited Authorized
                Delegates. \n(a) \nThe [appropriate court] in an action brought by
                a licensee shall have \njurisdiction to grant appropriate equitable
                or legal relief, including without limitation prohibiting \nthe authorized
                delegate from directly or indirectly acting as an authorized delegate
                for any licensee \nin this state and the payment of restitution, damages
                or other monetary relief, if the [appropriate \ncourt] finds that
                an authorized delegate failed to remit money in accordance with the
                written \ncontract required by [Section 8.01(b)] or as otherwise directed
                by the licensee or required by law. \n(b) \nIf the [appropriate court]
                issues an order prohibiting a person from acting as \nan authorized
                delegate for any licensee pursuant to [Section 8.03(a)], the licensee
                that brought the \naction shall report the order to the [Commissioner]
                within thirty (30) days and shall report the \norder through NMLS
                within ninety (90) days. \n(c) \nAn authorized delegate who holds
                money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly fails
                to remit more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference
                \nto state classification] felony. \n(d) \nAn authorized delegate
                who holds money in trust for the benefit of a \nlicensee and knowingly
                fails to remit no more than [$XXX] of such money is guilty of a [reference
                \nto state classification] misdemeanor. \nARTICLE IX  \nTimely Transmission,
                Refunds, and Disclosures \nSection 9.01 Timely Transmission. \n(a)
                \nEvery licensee shall forward all money received for transmission
                in \naccordance with the terms of the agreement between the licensee
                and the sender unless the licensee \nhas a reasonable belief or a
                reasonable basis to believe that the sender may be a victim of fraud
                or \nthat a crime or violation of law, rule, or regulation has occurred,
                is occurring, or may occur. \n(b) \nIf a licensee fails to forward
                money received for transmission in accordance \nwith this section,
                the licensee must respond to inquiries by the sender with the reason
                for the failure \n \n22 Commentary: An express trust account or segregated
                bank account is not required.\n"

              text: 'ey Transmitter License.


                Access to NMLS


                NMLS is a secure web-based system created by state regulators to provide
                efficiencies in the processing of state licenses and improve supervision
                of state-regulated industries.


                To access NMLS for the first time, you must complete a Company Account
                Request Form and identify a Primary Account Administrator and a Secondary
                Account Administrator. This form can be submitted online through the
                NMLS website in the Getting Started section. This form needs to be
                submitted only once per company, regardless of the number of NMLS
                participating states in which you are licensed.


                Within three days of completing and submitting the Company Account
                Request Form, the Primary Account Administrator will receive NMLS
                login information. The Primary Account Administrator will have full
                rights to access the system, submit information to this agency and
                other participating state regulators, and set up other company users
                in the system. Instructions and tutorials on how to access and use
                the system are also available in the NMLS Resource Center .


                Note : If your company already has a record in NMLS, you can omit
                this step.


                Managing Your License on NMLS


                Each company holding a DFS Money Transmitter License who wishes to
                manage their license on NMLS must create a company record in the system.
                To gain access to NMLS, the applicant must submit a form requesting
                an NMLS account.


                Current New York State Money Transmitters may transition their licenses
                to NMLS. See the DFS Money Transmitter Transition Checklist for more
                information.


                Submitting a Complete Application


                To submit an application and ensure your application is received,
                acknowledged as complete, and processed, please follow the instructions
                on the DFS Money Transmitter Checklists . No application shall be
                deemed to be complete until the Department has received all required
                information, documents, and fees.


                In the process of reviewing and considering the application, DFS may
                request additional information and supporting documents.


                In the application process, an NMLS Identification Number will be
                assigned to your application. Please maintain a record of this NMLS
                Identification Number, as it will be used as your application reference
                number throughout the remainder of the application process. The applicant’s
                NMLS Identification Number must be included on every hard-copy document
                submitted to the Department.


                Note : If the applicant has already submitted Forms MU1 and MU2 through
                NMLS for another state, the applicant does not need to re-enter the
                company record into NMLS. However, the applicant is required to provide
                jurisdiction-specific information to support its New York State application.


                Back to Top ▲


                Next Section


                Continue


                Annual Reporting


                The Annual Report should be prepared by qualified persons and submitted
                within 120 days following the close of the calendar year January 1
                to December 31, 2025.


                2025 NMLS Money Transmitter Annual Report Form


                2025 Non-NMLS Money Transmitter Annual Report Form


                Back to Top ▲


                Next Section


                Continue


                Reporting Change in Certain Individuals


                Pursuant to the following sections of the New York Banking Law (BL)
                and Superintendent’s Regulations (SR), licensees of the Department
                of Financial Services (DFS) are required to notify the Superintendent
                of changes in certain individuals, within stipulated time frames:


                Money Transmitters: BL 641, 642 and 652-a; and SR 406.11


                These requirements are for changes in certain individuals of licensees
                whose licenses are not managed on NMLS. For those managed on NMLS,
                visit the NMLS section website for New York State and navigate to
                Company Licenses and Amendment under the pertinent industry type,
                and look under Change in Control on the Amendment Checklist.


                Included Individuals


                Members of the governing board such as directors, trustees, and LLC
                members


                Officers (at a minimum Chief Executive Officer, President, Chief Financial
                Officer, Chief Compliance Officer, and Chief Operations Officer, and
                any other officers deemed necessary by DFS)


                Documentary requirements for Each Included Individual Being Added


                Notification on the licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized
                officer containing the following:


                Name and title of the individual being added


                Effective date of the addition


                Name and title of the person being replaced, and his/her new title/position,
                if any


                Resolution of the governing board approving the addition


                Personal Questionnaire (PDF)


                Fingerprints


                Background Investigation Report *


                Litigation Affidavit (PDF)


                Authority to Release Information (PDF)


                Resume


                Documentary requirements for Each Included Individual Being Removed:


                Notification on the licensee''s letterhead signed by an authorized
                officer containing the following:


                Name and title of the individual being removed


                Reason of the removal


                Effective date of the removal


                New title/position, if any


                Where To Submit?'

              text: 'How To Get A Money Transmitter License (MTL) in the U.S.


                Published Date  January 29, 2026


                To get a Money Transmitter License (MTL), businesses must undergo
                a rigorous application process that involves dual compliance with
                federal (like FinCEN''s AML/KYC protocols) and varying state-level
                regulations. Key requirements across states include demonstrating
                financial viability, often requiring a surety bond and capital reserves,
                passing comprehensive background checks for key personnel, and establishing
                a robust internal compliance program. The process is complex, time-consuming,
                and mandates extensive documentation and financial disclosures to
                ensure the applicant is law-abiding and financially sound.


                Operating a money transfer service in the U.S. involves tackling a
                myriad of federal and state laws, making how to get a money transmitter
                license both time-consuming and expensive. Compliance with agencies
                like FinCEN is non-negotiable to prevent illegal activities.


                Companies can either secure their own MSB license or partner with
                a licensed entity, but legal adherence is vital in both scenarios.
                It''s essential to understand what a money transmitter license is
                and who needs it.


                What is a Money Transmitter License?


                A Money Transmitter License is an official authorization or money
                service business license that empowers a firm or individual to facilitate
                the movement of capital. This license enables MSBs to handle financial
                transactions, ranging from digital payments to wire transfers.


                Possessing a Money Transmitter License brings forth substantial regulatory
                oversight. Organizations must prove they have the governance structure
                and internal controls to manage and safeguard client funds. States
                will continually scrutinize applicants, denying licensure to those
                who fail to meet the stringent criteria.


                In the United States, the need for a Money Transmitter License is
                not a choice; it''s a requirement for virtually any business involved
                in the handling or transferring of funds. Money transmitter license
                requirements by state can vary, so it''s crucial to be aware of the
                respective state money transmitter regulations.


                How to Get a Money Transmitter License?


                The license application process is designed to be rigorous, ensuring
                that approved businesses are law-abiding and financially sound. Federal
                and state-level regulations diverge, with each state setting its own
                financial criteria and often requiring a minimum capital commitment.


                Applicants typically need a surety bond of at least $500,000 per state,
                with costs influenced by credit history. The duration to obtain the
                license varies, contingent on the business type and the state of operation.


                Money Transmitter License Requirements


                Acquiring a money transmitter license involves compliance with Anti-Money
                Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) protocols. While these
                regulations are federal, individual states often impose additional
                requirements, thereby necessitating dual compliance.


                Subsequent to application submission, state authorities undertake
                an investigative review, focusing on financial sustainability and
                the applicant''s background.


                Standardized Requirements Across States


                Registration: Initial registration typically occurs with the Financial
                Crimes Enforcement Network or a similar state-level body.'
            source_version: 6ebc7b743e605b8e05363eb0628942c1

              path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-e6c1e4e85e004ccbe413/e06621859d4ec9431f2712a7c357b112/sections/s000001.md
              text: ', 2026


                Posted in Bank Regulatory


                On May 12, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) issued
                a significant interpretive letter confirming that Fidelity Digital
                Assets, National Association (the recently converted national trust
                bank formerly known as Fidelity Digital Assets Service, LLC) is not
                required to hold state money transmitter licenses to conduct its federally
                authorized activities. The OCC concluded that the National Bank Act
                preempts any state money transmitter licensing requirement as applied
                to a national bank.


                Until December 12, 2025, Fidelity Digital Assets operated as a New
                York-chartered limited liability trust company and held money transmitter
                licenses in numerous states, including Iowa. On that date, the OCC
                approved its conversion to an uninsured national trust bank under
                12 U.S.C. § 27(a). Concurrent with the conversion, the Bank surrendered
                its Iowa money transmitter license.


                Iowa pushed back. Its money transmitter statute exempts banks and
                trust companies from licensing, but only if they hold federally insured
                deposits. Because Fidelity Digital Assets is an uninsured national
                bank, Iowa argued the exemption did not apply and requested a legal
                basis for the license surrender. Fidelity Digital Assets responded
                that the National Bank Act preempts Iowa’s requirements and asked
                the OCC to confirm that position.


                The OCC’s analysis of whether a state can require a national bank
                to obtain a state money transmitter license as a condition of engaging
                in federally authorized activities, including cryptocurrency custody,
                trade execution, stablecoin issuance, and related digital asset services,
                rested on two independent and well-established pillars of federal
                banking law:


                1. National Bank Act Preemption


                Federal law authorizes national banks to conduct a broad range of
                activities on a national basis. Any state law that “prevents or significantly
                interferes” with a national bank’s exercise of its federally authorized
                powers is preempted.


                The OCC reasoned that requiring a national bank to obtain a state
                money transmitter license, even as a threshold condition to operating,
                would impermissibly condition the Bank’s federal authority on state
                approval. At the extreme, a state could veto federal authority outright
                by denying or revoking a license. Both outcomes are squarely preempted.
                This conclusion applies to any state’s money transmitter licensing
                regime, including states that limit their licensing exemptions to
                a subset of national banks (such as Iowa’s insured-deposits-only carveout).


                2. Exclusive Federal Visitorial Authority


                Separately, 12 U.S.C. § 484 vests the OCC with exclusive visitorial
                authority over national banks. “No national bank shall be subject
                to any visitorial powers except as authorized by Federal law.” Iowa’s
                money transmitter statute grants the state agency robust supervisory
                jurisdiction over licensees, including the power to demand books and
                records, conduct periodic examinations, take enforcement actions,
                and even place a licensee into receivership. Applying that regime
                to a national bank would be “fundamentally inconsistent” with the
                OCC’s exclusive visitorial powers and is therefore impermissible on
                independent grounds.


                Together, these two bases lead to a clean and sweeping conclusion:
                a national bank may conduct its federally authorized activities in
                any state without a state money transmitter license, regardless of
                whether it qualifies for any state-law exemption.


                Our Take


                The OCC’s conclusion here was entirely expected. The preemption framework
                for national banks is well-settled, and the OCC’s letter largely restates
                principles the Supreme Court and federal courts have applied for decades.
                That said, one nuance in this letter deserves closer attention: state-chartered
                trust banks are in a very different position.


                Unlike national banks, state trust companies and state-chartered banks
                do not benefit from National Bank Act preemption. Their ability to
                avoid state money transmitter licensing requirements depends entirely
                on how each individual state defines “bank” or “trust company” in
                its money transmission statute and those definitions vary considerably.


                Print:'
            source_version: e06621859d4ec9431f2712a7c357b112

        available_excerpt: "21 \n \nin a medium prescribed by the [Commissioner].
          The renewal report must state or contain a \ndescription of each material

          \napplication which has not been reported to the [Commissioner]. \n(c) \nThe
          [Commissioner] for good cause may grant an extension of the renewal \ndate.
          \n(d) \nThe [Commissioner] is authorized and encouraged to utilize NMLS
          to \nprocess license renewals provided that such functionality is consistent
          with this [Section 5.06]. \nSection 5.07 Maintenance of License. \n(a) \nIf
          a licensee does not continue to meet the qualifications or satisfy the \nrequirements
          that apply to an applicant for a new money transmission license, the [Commissioner]
          \nmay suspend or revoke the licensee's license in accordance with the procedures
          established by this \n[Act] or other applicable state law for such suspension
          or revocation. \n(b) \nAn applicant for a money transmission license must
          demonstrate that it \nmeets or will meet, and a money transmission licensee
          must at all times meet, the requirements in \n[Sections 10.01, 10.02, and
          10.03] of this [Act]. \nARTICLE VI \nAcquisition of Control and Change of
          Key Individual \nSection 6.01 Acquisition of Control. \n(a) \nAny person,
          or group of persons acting in concert, seeking to acquire control \nof a
          licensee shall obtain the written approval of the [Commissioner] prior to
          acquiring control. \nAn individual is not deemed to acquire control of a
          licensee and is not subject to these acquisition \nof control provisions
          when that individual becomes a key individual in the ordinary course of
          \nbusiness. \n(b) \nA person, or group of persons acting in concert, seeking
          to acquire control \nof a licensee shall, in cooperation with the licensee:
          \n(1) \nSubmit an application in a form and in a medium prescribed by the
          \n[Commissioner]; and \n(2) \nSubmit a nonrefundable fee of [$X] with the
          request for approval. \n(c) \nUpon request, the [Commissioner] may permit
          a licensee or the person, or \ngroup of persons acting in concert, to submit
          some or all information required by the \n[Commissioner] pursuant to [Section
          6.01(b)(1)] without using NMLS. \n(d) \nThe application required by [Section
          6.01(b)(1)] shall include information \nrequired by [Section 5.04] for any
          new key individuals that have not previously completed the \nrequirements
          of [Section 5.04] for a licensee.\n"

        source_version: dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a

        path: 03_Matters/harbor-2-d89ad8/research/source-library/SRC-37ee676da5b354ba8538/dd8e38dc121ab8ed7fe079b02c7e158a/pages/p000022.md
        source_hash: 175b57e812c71a8532569030d2db7113b5adc94e61bd9922dc0fee5d833c2748
        source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 22,
          characters 0–2612'
        unit_id: p000022
        locator: Page 22, characters 0–2612
        available_excerpt: "22 \n \n(e) \nWhen an application for acquisition of control
          under this [Section 6.01] \nappears to include all the items and address
          all of the matters that are required, the application shall \nbe considered
          complete and the [Commissioner] shall promptly notify the applicant in a
          record of \nthe date on which the application was determined to be complete
          and:15 \n \n(1) \nThe [Commissioner] shall approve or deny the application
          within 60 \ndays after the completion date; or \n(2) \nif the application
          is not approved or denied within 60 days after the \ncompletion date: \n(A)
          \nthe application is approved; and \n(B) \nthe person, or group of persons
          acting in concert, are not \nprohibited from acquiring control. \n(3) \nThe
          [Commissioner] may for good cause extend the application \nperiod. \n(f)
          \nA determination by the [Commissioner] that an application is complete
          and \nis accepted for processing means only that the application, on its
          face, appears to include all of the \nitems and address all of the matters
          that are required, and is not an assessment of the substance of \nthe application
          or of the sufficiency of the information provided. \n(g) \nWhen an application
          is filed and considered complete under [Section \n6.01(e)], the [Commissioner]
          shall investigate the financial condition and responsibility, financial
          \nand business experience, character, and general fitness of the person,
          or group of persons acting in \nconcert, seeking to acquire control. The
          [Commissioner] shall approve an acquisition of control \npursuant to this
          [Section 6.01] if the [Commissioner] finds that all of the following conditions
          have \nbeen fulfilled: \n(1) \nThe requirements of subsections (b) and (d)
          have been met, as \napplicable; and \n(2) \nthe financial condition and
          responsibility, financial and business \nexperience, competence, character,
          and general fitness of the person, or group of persons \nacting in concert,
          seeking to acquire control; and the competence, experience, character, \nand
          general fitness of the key individuals and persons that would be in control
          of the \nlicensee after the acquisition of control indicate that it is in
          the interest of the public to \npermit the person, or group of persons acting
          in concert, to control the licensee. \n(h) \nIf an applicant avails itself
          or is otherwise subject to a multistate licensing \n \n15 Commentary: NMLS
          will accommodate and streamline the process of communicating when applications
          are \nreceived and when states consider them to have been complete. The
          intent of this Act is for the application period to \nbegin on the day an
          application is determined to be complete.\n"

        source_label: '[PDF] CSBS Money Transmission Modernization Act — Page 23,
